memory_candidates.content: Typst figures (#figure blocks) are atomic and do NOT break across pages by default, so a table taller than one page overflows off the bottom and later rows overlap/collide instead of continuing. Fix: add `#show figure: set block(breakable: true)`. Additionally, `columns: (auto, ...)` lets a wide first column starve the rest; long unbreakable monospace tokens (file paths, `[Ident T]`) overflow into the next column. For A4 with wide margins, prefer 2 columns (merge description columns) and shorten path prefixes. Always render pages to PNG (pdftoppm) and inspect visually — Typst does not warn about table overflow.

Typst bundles 'New Computer Modern' and 'New Computer Modern Math' as built-in fonts (verify with `typst fonts | grep -i 'new computer modern'`), so documents using `#set text(font: "New Computer Modern")` compile without external font install even when fc-list shows nothing. However thmbox 0.3.0's default theorem-title fonts request 'New Computer Modern Sans' (NOT bundled), producing two benign 'unknown font family' warnings that fall back cleanly. Also: `typst compile out.pdf` fails with 'No such file or directory' if the target directory (e.g. build/) does not exist — Typst does not create it; mkdir first.

In Typst table/grid cells, a cell whose content string begins with `+ ` or `- ` is parsed as a list/enum item and renders as '1.' or a bullet. To show a literal leading '+ classicality' in a cell, reword (e.g. 'least, and classical') or escape the leading marker.
